Pauline Hanson says under their plan anyone paying rent or a mortgage can take up to a quarter of their super as a “pay boost” for up to three years. Continue reading...

Albanese government ministers are comparing opposition to internet users taking control of social media algorithms to protesting the introduction of seatbelts, as a battle brews in Canberra.

In coming days, the federal government will unveil legislation that would allow people to opt out of algorithms dictated by social media giants.

But the plan has already been criticised by the Coalition, which has called the idea overreach and said it could amount to censorship.

Health Minister Mark Butler said the change was crucial to keeping people safe online.

“It’s pretty unremarkable really to expect that big companies have a duty of care not to harm Australian citizens, particularly, frankly, young Australians.”

Communications Minister Anika Wells said people online needed greater control over what they saw on their social media feeds.

“We want to hold big tech to account. We want them to observe the same basic safety standards, particularly for our children,” she told ABC TV.

“If you walk down the toy aisle in Big W and you see plastic toys, electronic toys and iPads, you want all of those manufacturers to have abided by basic safety standards when they’re selling something to our kids, and that’s what big tech should have.”
